soṇakāyana.notes: Sikhāmoggallāna reports the student's accusation in AN 4.234. AN 4.233 shares the page. AN 4.242 names Soṇakāyana in the chapter recap.

soṇā.notes: AN 1.241 singles out the energetic nun. In Thig 5.8 she recalls bearing ten children and going forth in old age. AN 8.91–117 lists the laywoman and her mother separately. AN 6.55 and Ud 5.6 address men called Soṇa, as do SN 22.49, SN 22.50 and SN 35.128. The adjacent AN 1 groups and AN 8.118–119 are page overlaps.

subha.notes: DN 10, MN 99 and MN 135 each call the student Todeyya's son. His conversation with Jāṇussoṇi is in MN 99.30. The references placed in MN 29–30 miss that episode. MN 116 lists an independent Buddha. Thig 13.5 and 14.1 name nuns called Subhā.

subhadda.notes: DN 16 has all three men. The deceased lay follower appears at 2.6.13, the wanderer who gains ordination at 5.23–30, and the monk who welcomes the Buddha's death at 6.20. A single entry for the whole sutta would misidentify the other two. SN 55.10 names the deceased non-returner at Ñātika. The placement in SN 55.5–6 misses him. DN 17 names Queen Subhaddā.

subhagavana.notes: DN 14, MN 1 and MN 49 locate the forest at Ukkaṭṭhā. The entry cites SN 6.4 for a parallel Baka episode whose setting is Jeta's Grove. SN 6.3 concerns Brahmadeva.

subhā.notes: DPD's THI71 is the nun of Jīvaka's mango grove in Thig 14.1. Thig 13.5 names the smith's daughter. Neither has a candidate biography. MN 120.20.6–8 names all three classes of gods in the entry under their individual names. The packet also picks up the male student in DN 10 and MN 99.

subāhu.notes: Thag 1.52 is Subāhu's own rain verse. Its Pali attribution joins the name and title as Subāhutthero, and the packet omits it. The separate name in the recap at Thag 1.60:2.1 identifies the elder alongside Godhika. The main verse of Thag 1.60 belongs to Sīvali.

sucimukhī.notes: The wanderer questions Sāriputta about the direction he faces while eating in SN 28.10. SN 28.8–9 are conversations with Ānanda.

sucitti.notes: DN 20.12 names Sucitti among the asuras. Sujato reads Dānava and Ghasa as separate names in the preceding line, so the subgroup claimed in the entry is uncertain.

sudassana.notes: Pasenadi asks the student to repeat the verse at meals in SN 3.13. SN 3.14 concerns a battle. MN 116.4.5 explicitly names an independent Buddha who lived on Isigili. Neither candidate describes the mountain by Lake Anottatta.

sudatta.notes: The donor's biography is filed separately as Anāthapiṇḍika 01. AN 1.249 and SN 10.8 explicitly equate the names. SN 10.12 recaps SN 10.8. DN 16 and SN 55.8 identify the deceased once-returner at Ñātika. SN 55.7 is a page overlap. Sudatta 07 is the godling in SN 2.16, called Vāsudatta in the app and Sudatta in the Pali edition cited (SN I 53). The godling speaks the first stanza and the Buddha replies with the second. Thag 1.37 identifies the elder in Sudatta 11 by his epithet, Kumāputta's friend.

suddhikabhāradvāja.notes: SN 7.7 names the brahmin who asks about purity. SN 7.5 and SN 7.6 concern other brahmins.

sujāta.notes: Thig 13.4 recounts the journey to Mithilā and names Sundarī's father Sujāta at 11.3, 12.5 and 13.5. The English gives his name one segment later each time, so the packet misses him. SN 21.5 praises a monk called Sujāta. DPPN itself treats his identification with the father as conjectural. SN 21.4 concerns an unnamed junior monk. The other packet hits are women called Sujātā. No candidate describes the previous Buddha.

sujātā.notes: AN 1.258 names Seniyadhītā as first to go for refuge. The Sujātā named in DN 16:2.6–7 is the stream-enterer from Ñātika, also named in SN 55.8. DN 16:4.42 mentions the meal before awakening but leaves its donor unnamed. AN 7.63 identifies Anāthapiṇḍika's daughter-in-law. AN 7.62, SN 55.7 and the flanking AN 1 groups are page overlaps. Thig 6.4 attributes its verses to the nun, who has no candidate biography.

sukkā.notes: DN 20:17.1 explicitly lists the Sukkā gods. Sujato translates the name as ‘the gods of Venus’, so the packet misses this identification. SN 10.8 is about Sudatta. The nun is the preacher in SN 10.9 and the recipient of a meal in SN 10.10. The chapter recap at SN 10.12:14.4 also refers to her two discourses.

sumana.notes: AN 6.49 names Khema and Sumana together in the Dark Forest. The citation lands in AN 6.44. DPPN offers two possible identifications for Khema's companion, and neither Thag 5.4 nor Thag 6.10 ties its speaker to Khema. DN 32 lists the yakkha chief beside Pajjunna and Sumukha. The feminine Sumanā in the AN and Thig passages belongs to a separate name.

sumanā.notes: The full entry describes the princess of AN 5.31 and explicitly cites verse 16 for the nun ordained in old age (Thig 1.16). It attributes the link between their lives to the commentary. Thig 1.14 is a separate attribution. AN 8.91–117 names a laywoman without her royal title. SN 3.1 names Pasenadi, while the commentary places Sumanā there. AN 5.30 and AN 8.89–90 are page overlaps. AN 6.49 names a male elder.

sumbha.notes: All three SN settings place the town in the land of the Sumbhas. Its name is Setaka in the Pali of SN 46.30 and Sedaka in SN 47.19–20. The entry gives ‘Desaka (?)’. SN 46.29 is a page overlap.

sunakkhatta.notes: The entry reverses Sunakkhatta's statement in MN 12:2.5. He denies the Buddha's superhuman knowledge but affirms that practicing the teaching leads to the ending of suffering. The Buddha repeats that concession at 4.3–5. MN 11 is a page overlap. MN 110:26.2 also names the Sunakkhatta discourse in its chapter recap.
